completionOptions.mergeCommitMessage:
Merged PR 2842: refactor(tm-federation): extract HC listener into dedicated Bridge service

Problem

The HC listener lives inside Leo.Cars.Raptor.Federation.TM.Api, which couples the customer host's public ingress (the relay listener) to the federation HTTP API. We want a separate Bridge process so the API can be restarted/updated/health-probed by an isolated supervisor (the planned /tm-admin/* endpoints), and so the customer host has a single dedicated process for relay connectivity.

Solution

New project Leo.Cars.Raptor.Federation.TM.Bridge (ASP.NET Core, .NET 10) becomes the HC listener and a path-routed forwarder. Federation.TM.Api loses the listener and binds loopback-only; Bridge is the single public ingress.

Path-routed forwarder in the listener (no separate middleware): on each relayed request the listener inspects the path:

  • /tm-admin/* → BridgeLoopback HttpClient → Bridge's own Kestrel on 127.0.0.1:<LocalForwardingPort>. Admin endpoints get full ASP.NET Core treatment (routing, future auth, model binding).
  • Everything else → FederationApi HttpClient → Federation API. Hot path is a single HTTP hop.

Forwarding logic lives in one place (the listener); the dedicated forwarder middleware that initially existed was removed to avoid duplicating the header copy + stream handling. Hop-by-hop headers stripped, body streamed with HttpCompletionOption.ResponseHeadersRead.

Three /tm-admin/* endpoints (POST /update, GET /health, POST /restart) ship as 501 stubs. Real implementations land in follow-ups once the auth scheme is settled.

Fail-fast at startup: if HybridConnectionListener.OpenAsync throws, the listener logs Critical and throws InvalidOperationException. The .NET 6+ default BackgroundServiceExceptionBehavior.StopHost tears the host down so Windows Service Manager sees a Failed state. No more log-and-idle mode -- Bridge has no useful behaviour without an open listener.

Enabled flag removed from ListenerHybridConnectionOptions: the Bridge is purpose-built for HC; running it with HC disabled would be a configuration mistake.

DPAPI key resolution: KeyValueFilePath support carries over -- the MSI installer (separate PR) writes a DPAPI-encrypted SAS blob and the Bridge decrypts it at startup with machine scope.

Scalar UI mounted at /scalar/v1 on the Bridge's loopback port, on-box only (HC never forwards /scalar or /openapi here).

Federation.TM.Api cleanup: HC listener + options moved (git detects rename); HC-conditional HttpClient + Kestrel binding block removed from Program.cs
